why:
see `rust:LifecyclePollingNode`. This is rclcpp's word for the operation, and it is public here -- as it now is in our C++ (`nros::LifecycleNode::trigger_transition`, public since phase 379 W5; this row used to say `protected trigger()`), and as `rclc_lifecycle_state_machine_change_state` in our C. All three take the same `lifecycle_msgs/msg/Transition` ids since issue 1099; before it, the C and C++ entry points took nano-ros's own numbering, which disagreed with upstream on four of eight values. NOTE: the correlator never emitted a `cpp:LifecycleNode::trigger_transition` row -- the same blind spot that let the id divergence through (`correlate.py:compare()` matches on name and arity and never on VALUES) -- so phase-428 W5 authored one by hand; the id-space defect and its fix are recorded THERE.

NO DISPOSITION IS WRITTEN on this row. The four dispositions are what clause 1 does to a CANDIDATE FROM CLAUSE 2 (RFC-0089), and rclrs ships no lifecycle support, so this item has no upstream candidate.
